newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power trades thinly over a wide range.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power trades thinly over a wide range.

text.p: Spot bulk power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) traded thinly over a wide range Wednesday with power demand said to be low in the state, brokers and marketers said.
"The loads have fallen way off," said one ERCOT marketer.

Forecasts called for temperatures in the high 50s and low 60s degrees Fahrenheit on Thursday, while on Friday temperatures in the southern half of the state were expected to be near normal and two to four degrees above normal in the north and west.
By Sunday, temperatures through much of the state were expected to be five to 15 degrees above normal and possibly higher.

ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Thursday delivery was said to have traded over a wide range of $24.50-30.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $30.00-33.00 on Tuesday for Wednesday delivery, the sources said.
Non-firm on peak power for Wednesday was notionally pegged at $21.00-24.00 from a notional Tuesday assessment at $27.00-30.00, the sources said.
Firm off-peak Thursday ERCOT deliveries were notionally assessed lower at $14.00-18.00 from $18.00-20.00 on Tuesday, with very little business said to be done.
Non firm off peak power was notionally pegged lower at $11.00-14.00 from $15.00-17.00 per MWh.
February ERCOT peak power was assessed steady at $27.00-27.60, the sources said.
